gauge-pressure: Pressure measured above the pressure of the air around us, as a tyre gauge reads it. This book uses it throughout, so the surface of still water is at zero and each metre below it adds about 9.8 kPa.
gravity-dam: A concrete or masonry dam that holds back its water by its own weight, pressing down on the rock beneath it. In section it is close to a triangle: wide at the foot, narrow at the top.
kilopascal: The unit of pressure in this book: one kilonewton spread over one square metre. Still water adds about 9.8 kPa for every metre of depth; the air around us presses with about 101 kPa.

entry: The pressure in still water. At any point it is the same in every direction, and it depends only on the depth, p = ρgh, about 9.8 kPa per metre. Water in the ground follows the same rule only while it is not flowing.
